gaps.sentence: ___ Hyde Park is lovely in autumn.
gaps.explanation: Most park names take no article: Hyde Park, Central Park (exception: the Grands Boulevards style names).

gaps.sentence: ___ curiosity killed the cat, as they say.
gaps.explanation: 'Curiosity' as an abstract quality takes no article, even in the proverb.

gaps.sentence: The novel had a huge effect on ___ young people of the 1960s.
gaps.explanation: 'The young people of the 1960s' — defined by the of-phrase, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: ___ honesty is the best policy, as the saying goes.
gaps.explanation: Abstract nouns used in a general sense take no article: honesty, happiness, love.

gaps.sentence: ___ honest answer would have saved everyone time.
They drove to ___ south of France for the summer.
gaps.explanation: 'By train' takes no article; 'the south of France' takes 'the' (compass areas).
Both 'happiness' and 'money' are general here, so no article for either gap.

gaps.sentence: He had ___ operation on his knee last year.
gaps.explanation: 'Operation' starts with a vowel sound, so 'an operation'.
